# Docker-BuildAgent

[![CI](https://github.com/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Build](https://github.com/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent?logo=semver&logoColor=white&label=Version)](https://github.com/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent/releases/latest)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue?logo=opensourceinitiative&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-Live-blue?logo=gitbook&logoColor=white)](https://build-agent.subzerodev.com)

Docker-BuildAgent is a container image that carries the tooling for building JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js, Angular, .NET and PowerShell projects, plus a build command (`build`) that runs a standard build for your project. Use it in GitHub Actions or any other CI system that can run a container.

Canonical contract (image, build command, Docker-template discovery): [design/20-contract.md](https://github.com/The-Running-Dev/Docker-BuildAgent/blob/main/design/20-contract.md)

## What the image contains

- Base image `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/javascript-node:22-bookworm` (Node.js 22 and npm), overridable with the `BASE_IMAGE` build argument
- TypeScript, tsx and the Angular CLI
- PowerShell, which is the default shell
- The Docker CLI with the Buildx and Compose plugins
- .NET SDKs 8, 9 and 10, Git, GitVersion and the NUKE global tool
- The `build` command, which takes one of five build types: `docker`, `node`, `node-in-docker`, `node-template` and `forge`

The working directory is `/workspace`. The image is published as `ghcr.io/the-running-dev/build-agent`. `latest` moves on every push to `main` and on every release; a versioned tag is written only by a release.

## Choose a build

The `build` command has five types: `docker`, `node`, `node-in-docker`, `node-template` and `forge`. Which one suits your project, and what each needs (the Docker host, project files, CI tokens), is in [Build Types](https://build-agent.subzerodev.com/docs/build-types#choose-a-build).

## Prerequisites

- **Docker**, running. Every build runs in the image. [What each build needs](https://build-agent.subzerodev.com/docs/build-types#what-each-build-needs) says which builds also need the Docker host.
- To work on this repository you also need the .NET 8 SDK, PowerShell and the `docs-template/` submodule (`git clone --recurse-submodules`). The first check there needs no Docker host: `dotnet run --project forge/DocsCheck -c Release -- .`

## Quick start

Mount your project at `/workspace` and run a build type. This builds a Docker image from your project (mount the Docker socket so the container can reach the Docker host):

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
    -v "${PWD}:/workspace" \
    -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
    ghcr.io/the-running-dev/build-agent:latest \
    build docker
```

The other build types work the same way:

```bash
# Build a Node.js application
docker run --rm -it \
    -v "${PWD}:/workspace" \
    ghcr.io/the-running-dev/build-agent:latest \
    build node

# Build a Node.js application and package it as a Docker image
docker run --rm -it \
    -v "${PWD}:/workspace" \
    -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
    ghcr.io/the-running-dev/build-agent:latest \
    build node-in-docker

# Generate a changelog from Git history
docker run --rm -it \
    -v "${PWD}:/workspace" \
    ghcr.io/the-running-dev/build-agent:latest \
    build forge --change-log-source all
```

If your project has no `Dockerfile`, the agent looks for a matching template; see [Docker Templates](https://build-agent.subzerodev.com/docs/docker-templates).

## Use it in GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Container-CI

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  packages: write
  contents: write

jobs:
  Container-CI:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/the-running-dev/build-agent:latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Container CI
        run: build docker
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RegistryToken: ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
```

`RegistryToken` is the token the build uses to push the image to your registry (for GHCR, a token with the `write:packages` scope). The push runs only on a CI server and not in a dry run (the `ForcePush` parameter overrides both). See [Parameters](https://build-agent.subzerodev.com/docs/parameters) for every setting.

## Build the image from this repository

You need Docker and a .NET SDK that can build .NET 8 projects. The `Dockerfile` copies the compiled Forge build system from `artifacts/`, which is not in the repository, and the `docs-template/` submodule, so clone with submodules and build the image through one of the scripts, which compile Forge into `artifacts/` first and then run the `docker` build type:

```pwsh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/the-running-dev/Docker-BuildAgent
cd Docker-BuildAgent

# Windows, or anywhere PowerShell runs
./build.ps1
```

```sh
# Linux, macOS, CI
./build.sh
```

Run locally, neither script pushes anything: the registry push is skipped on a developer machine unless `ForcePush` is set. `build.ps1` accepts `-type` to run another build type (for example `./build.ps1 -type node`) and forwards any other argument to the build, such as `--image-tag myapp:v1.0.0`. `build.sh` always runs the `docker` build type and passes its arguments to it.

## Repository layout

```text
Dockerfile                 the image definition
build.ps1, build.sh        local build scripts: compile Forge, then run a build type
GitVersion.yml             GitVersion configuration
forge/                     the Forge build system (.NET, NUKE), one project per concern
  Common/                    shared services, components and parameters
  Config/                    the project configuration file
  Docker/  Node/  NodeInDocker/  Forge/
                             the build types (Forge is the changelog build)
  Surface/                   the public-surface manifest and compatibility gate
  Release/                   the release pipeline
  Update/  Tool/             the container update and rollback library and its command
  DocsCheck/                 checks the documentation against the code
  *.Tests/                   the test projects
scripts/
  nuke/                      the `build` command inside the image, including node-template
  powershell-module/         the Docker-BuildAgent PowerShell module
templates/                 built-in Dockerfile templates (Angular, Node)
samples/                   sample project configuration files, one per build type
documentation/             the documentation site sources
docs-template/             the pinned Docusaurus-Template submodule that builds the site
design/                    the design chain and the contract (design/20-contract.md)
PSModule.requirements.md   the PowerShell module contract
.github/                   workflows and shared actions
changelog.ps1              regenerates CHANGELOG.md from the Git history
scripts/build-docs-local.ps1   previews the documentation site with hot reload
docs.ps1, docs-image.ps1   older preview helpers, not the supported flow
```
